title: Kit (formerly ConvertKit) Review 2026: Is This the Best Email Marketing Platform for Creators?
content:
*Affiliate disclosure: Some links in this article are affiliate links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. This never affects our ratings or recommendations. [Full disclosure](/disclosure)*

**Last updated: June 20, 2026**

## Quick Answer

**Kit (formerly ConvertKit) is the best email marketing platform for creators in 2026** — authors, bloggers, podcasters, YouTubers, and course builders who want to build genuine relationships with their audience without fighting complex marketing automation tools. With a clean, tag-based subscriber management system, stunning landing pages, industry-leading deliverability rates of ~97%, and a free plan that supports up to 1,000 subscribers, Kit delivers exactly what creators need and nothing they don't. Plans start at **$0/month** (Free Newsletter plan) and scale to **$66/month** (Pro) for 1,000 base subscribers. The platform now supports Visual Automations, SMS marketing, a newsletter site builder, and the innovative Kit MCP (AI-powered content creation). However, if you need advanced CRM, complex multi-step automation waterfalls, or flashy email templates, ActiveCampaign or Mailchimp may be better options.

---

---

## Pros and Cons

### Pros 👍

- **Creator-first design philosophy** — Kit was built by a creator (Nathan Barry) for creators. Every feature, from tagging to automations to landing pages, is optimized for people who sell courses, books, memberships, and digital products. There's no enterprise bloat or unnecessary complexity.
- **Brilliant tagging system** — Instead of confusing lists-within-segments-within-audiences, Kit uses simple tags. Any subscriber gets any tag for any action. It's intuitive, flexible, and infinitely scalable. This single design decision saves creators hours of list management every month.
- **Stunning landing pages** — The landing page builder produces beautiful, high-converting opt-in pages in under five minutes. No coding required. Unlimited landing pages even on the free plan. This alone makes Kit worth considering.
- **Free plan up to 1,000 subscribers** — A full-featured free tier with unlimited landing pages, forms, email broadcasts, audience tagging, and the ability to sell digital products. No credit card required. This is the most generous free plan in the industry for creators.
- **Industry-leading deliverability (~97%)** — Kit maintains an excellent sender reputation with automatic list hygiene, engagement-based sending, and proactive inbox placement monitoring. Your emails actually reach your audience.
- **Recommendations feature** — An innovative cross-promotion tool that lets other creators recommend your newsletter to their audience. It's like affiliate marketing for email list growth, and users report adding thousands of subscribers through it.
- **Newsletter site (micro-website)** — Every Kit account comes with a beautiful, customizable newsletter site that serves as a destination for all your content. No separate website builder needed.
- **Visual Automations** — The drag-and-drop automation builder lets you create welcome sequences, product launch funnels, and re-engagement campaigns without touching code. Creators using automations see 3.2x faster list growth.
- **Digital product sales built-in** — Sell products, subscriptions, and paid newsletters directly from Kit with built-in payment processing via Stripe. No third-party platform required.
- **Free migrations** — Kit offers free, assisted migrations from Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, and other platforms. Their team handles the heavy lifting.

### Cons 👎

- **No built-in CRM** — Unlike ActiveCampaign or HubSpot, Kit has no deal tracking, pipeline management, or sales automation. It's an email marketing tool, not a CRM. Growing creators who need sales pipeline features will need a separate CRM.
- **Minimal email design options** — If you want flashy, multi-column, heavily branded email templates, Kit is not for you. The platform prioritizes plain-text readability and single-column layouts. This approach gets better open rates but limits brand expression in emails.
- **Limited analytics** — Reporting covers the essentials (opens, clicks, subscriber growth) but lacks advanced features like revenue attribution, heatmaps, click maps, predictive scoring, and detailed geolocation data. Pro plan adds better analytics but still trails ActiveCampaign.
- **No A/B testing on lower plans** — Subject line A/B testing requires the Creator plan ($33/mo). Content A/B testing is locked behind the Pro plan ($66/mo). Competitors offer A/B testing on cheaper tiers.
- **Automation depth is simpler** — While Kit's Visual Automations are intuitive and effective, they lack the depth of ActiveCampaign's conditional logic, split paths, predictive triggers, and goal-based funnels. Power users may feel constrained.
- **Pricing jumps as you grow** — At 1,000 subscribers Kit is affordable ($33/mo Creator), but the price increases proportionally with your list size. At 10,000 subscribers, Creator jumps to roughly $83/mo, and at 100,000 subscribers it reaches $350+/mo. Still competitive, but the jump surprises some creators.
- **No native e-commerce CRM** — While Kit integrates with Shopify and has basic purchase tracking, it lacks the deep e-commerce automation and product recommendation features of Klaviyo or Mailchimp's advanced e-commerce tools.

---

## What is Kit (formerly ConvertKit)?

Kit is an email marketing platform designed specifically for **creators** — a term that encompasses bloggers, authors, podcasters, YouTubers, course creators, and anyone building an audience online. Founded in 2013 by Nathan Barry (author of *The App Design Handbook* and *Authority*), the platform was originally named ConvertKit and built to solve the email marketing needs of creators who found Mailchimp too complex and ActiveCampaign too enterprise-focused.

In 2025, ConvertKit rebranded to **Kit**, a shorter, more memorable name that reflects the platform's evolution from a simple email tool into a complete creator business operating system. Despite the name change, the core philosophy remains unchanged: give creators the simplest possible tools to grow their audience, monetize their following, and build lasting relationships through email.

Kit now serves **hundreds of thousands of creators** worldwide, powers billions of emails annually, and has helped creators earn over **$1 billion** in revenue through its platform. Notable users include best-selling authors, top podcasters, and successful course creators.

The platform recently launched several significant features in 2026:
- **Kit MCP** (Model Context Protocol) — AI-powered content creation that integrates with AI coding tools
- **Enhanced Visual Automations** — More powerful workflow builder with branching logic
- **SMS Marketing** — Reach subscribers via text messages (Creator plan and above)
- **Newsletter Sites** — Full micro-website for your content
- **Advanced Subscriber Signals** — Engagement scoring and predictive analytics (Pro plan)

---

## Detailed Feature Analysis

### 1. Email Creation & User Experience (95/100)

Kit's email editor is refreshingly minimal. There are no cluttered toolbars, no overwhelming template galleries, no decision paralysis. You get a clean writing interface, basic formatting options, and the ability to add images, buttons, and links. That's it. And that's exactly what most creators want.

The editor supports two modes:
- **Rich Text** — For styled emails with images, buttons, and formatting
- **Plain Text** — For personal, conversational emails that feel like direct messages

This simplicity is intentional. Research consistently shows that plain-text and simple single-column emails get higher open and click-through rates than heavily designed HTML emails. Kit's approach forces good email practices by default.

**What sets Kit apart:**
- **Subscriber preview** — See exactly how your email looks for any subscriber, with their name, custom fields, and tags applied
- **Send time optimization** — Kit automatically schedules emails for when individual subscribers are most likely to engage
- **Conditional content** — Show different content blocks to different segments within the same email
- **Instant broadcast preview** — See how your email renders on desktop and mobile before sending

The overall user experience is best-in-class for creators. The dashboard shows your subscriber count, recent growth, and key metrics at a glance. Navigation is intuitive, with clear paths to broadcasts, sequences, automations, landing pages, and subscribers.

### 2. Automation Capabilities (88/100)

Kit's Visual Automation builder is where the platform has made the most progress. The drag-and-drop interface allows you to create complex subscriber journeys without any coding knowledge.

**What you can automate:**
- **Welcome sequences** — Automatically send a series of emails when someone subscribes
- **Lead magnet delivery** — Deliver free downloads, checklists, or guides when subscribers join your list
- **Product launch funnels** — Build anticipation with pre-launch, launch, and post-launch sequences
- **Abandon cart reminders** — Automatically follow up with subscribers who added products but didn't purchase
- **Re-engagement campaigns** — Win back inactive subscribers with targeted content
- **Upsell sequences** — Recommend additional products based on past purchases
- **Birthday/anniversary emails** — Send personalized greetings automatically

**Automation triggers include:**
- Subscriber joins a form or landing page
- Subscriber clicks a specific link
- Subscriber purchases a product
- Subscriber is tagged with a specific tag
- Subscriber is added to or removed from a sequence
- Subscriber reaches a specific engagement score
- Custom date or time-based triggers

According to Kit's internal data, creators who use Visual Automations grow their lists **3.2x faster** and generate an average of **$42 more per automated workflow** compared to those who only send broadcast emails. The "24/7" nature of automations means your business keeps working even while you sleep, travel, or focus on content creation.

**Limitations:** Compared to ActiveCampaign's automation engine, Kit's builder is simpler. ActiveCampaign supports goal-based funnels (where the automation automatically optimizes toward a conversion goal), predictive triggers (using AI to determine the best send time), split-path testing within automations, and CRM-based triggers. Kit's automations are linear and trigger-based, which covers 90% of creator use cases but falls short for complex multi-product sales funnels.

### 3. Pricing & Value (94/100)

Kit offers three pricing tiers, all based on your subscriber count:

| Plan | Monthly Price | Yearly Price | Key Features |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Newsletter (Free)** | $0/mo | $0/yr | Up to 1,000 subs, 1 basic automation, unlimited landing pages & forms, unlimited broadcasts, tagging, sell digital products |
| **Creator** | $33/mo | $390/yr ($32.50/mo) | Unlimited automations, email sequences, A/B test subject lines, SMS marketing, Kit MCP, Remove Kit branding, Apps & integrations, RSS campaigns, priority support |
| **Pro** | $66/mo | $790/yr ($65.83/mo) | Subscriber Signals, engagement analytics, unlimited users, insights dashboard, deliverability reporting, subscriber scoring, A/B test subject lines & content, collaborative editing, Facebook custom audiences, newsletter referral system |

**Value analysis:** Kit's free plan is the most generous in the industry for creators. Mailchimp's free plan limits you to 500 subscribers with restricted features. ActiveCampaign's free plan is very limited. Kit gives you full access to landing pages, forms, tags, broadcasts, and digital product sales for up to 1,000 subscribers at zero cost.

At the Creator level ($33/mo), you get unlimited automations, SMS marketing, and the ability to remove Kit branding. This is excellent value compared to Mailchimp's Standard plan ($20/mo for only 500 subs) or ActiveCampaign's Plus plan ($49/mo for 1,000 subs).

The Pro plan ($66/mo) adds analytics depth, team collaboration, and advanced A/B testing. It's competitively priced against Mailchimp's Premium ($59/mo for 500 subs) and ActiveCampaign's Pro ($79/mo for 1,000 subs).

**The pricing scales proportionally with your list size:**
- 1,000 subs: $33/mo (Creator)
- 5,000 subs: ~$59/mo (Creator)
- 10,000 subs: ~$83/mo (Creator)
- 25,000 subs: ~$167/mo (Creator)
- 100,000 subs: ~$350/mo (Creator)

This is transparent and predictable. No hidden fees, no email send limits (unlike Mailchimp's contact-based tiers with send caps).

### 4. Landing Pages & Forms (96/100)

This is arguably Kit's strongest feature. The landing page builder is genuinely best-in-class for creators who want beautiful, high-converting opt-in pages without hiring a designer or developer.

**Key features:**
- **Professionally designed templates** — 20+ templates optimized for email capture, product sales, webinar registration, and content upgrades
- **Drag-and-drop editor** — Rearrange sections, change colors, add images, and customize text without any coding
- **Unlimited pages** — Create as many landing pages and forms as you need, even on the free plan
- **Custom domains** — Use your own domain (e.g., freebie.yourbrand.com) for professional branding
- **GDPR compliance built-in** — Automatic consent checkboxes and data processing agreements
- **Conversion analytics** — See views, conversions, and conversion rates for every page and form
- **A/B testing** — Test different headlines, images, and layouts (Pro plan)
- **Embeddable forms** — Add signup forms to your existing website with a simple embed code or WordPress plugin
- **Inline forms** — Place forms directly within email content for seamless subscriber capture

Creators report conversion rates of 20-40% on Kit landing pages, significantly above the industry average of 10-15%. The clean, mobile-responsive designs and fast loading times contribute to these exceptional results.

### 5. Deliverability (97/100)

Email deliverability is arguably the most important metric for any email marketing platform. What good is a beautifully written email if it lands in the spam folder?

Kit consistently achieves **~97% inbox placement rates**, putting it among the top performers in the industry. Here's how they do it:

- **Clean sender reputation** — Kit proactively monitors sender reputation across major ISPs (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, etc.) and alerts you if anything needs attention
- **Automatic list hygiene** — Kit automatically suppresses hard bounces, unengaged subscribers, and invalid email addresses to maintain list quality
- **Authentication protocols** — Full support for SPF, DKIM, and DMARC authentication to verify sender identity
- **Engagement-based sending** — The platform prioritizes sending to engaged subscribers, naturally improving deliverability
- **Warm-up tools** — For new senders, Kit provides guidance on gradually increasing send volume to build reputation
- **Proactive monitoring** — On the Pro plan, you get detailed deliverability reporting with inbox placement rates by provider

This focus on deliverability means your carefully crafted emails actually reach your audience. For creators whose income depends on email engagement, this is invaluable.

### 6. Integrations & Ecosystem (88/100)

Kit connects with **100+ apps and platforms** through its App Store, plus thousands more through Zapier and the Kit API.

**Notable native integrations:**
- **Shopify** — Automatically tag subscribers who purchase, trigger abandoned cart sequences, and track product revenue
- **Thinkific & Teachable** — Sync course enrollments, tag students, and automate course launch sequences
- **Stripe** — Direct payment processing for product sales
- **WordPress** — Plugin for embedding signup forms
- **Calendly** — Trigger automations based on booked calls
- **Linktree** — Add email signup to your Linktree page
- **Mighty Networks** — Sync community members with your email list
- **Zapier** — Connect to 5,000+ apps for unlimited workflow possibilities
- **REST API** — Full programmatic access for custom integrations

The Kit App Store is growing rapidly, with new integrations added regularly. The 2026 addition of **Kit MCP** (Model Context Protocol) is particularly innovative — it allows AI coding tools like Claude, Cursor, and Copilot to directly interact with Kit, enabling automated content creation, subscriber management, and analytics retrieval through natural language.

**Limitation:** While 100+ native integrations is solid, it trails ActiveCampaign's 870+ native integrations and Mailchimp's marketplace ecosystem. For most creators, however, the available integrations cover the essential tools needed to run a creator business.

### 7. Analytics & Reporting (83/100)

Kit's analytics are functional but minimal compared to competitors. This is a deliberate trade-off — Kit prioritizes simplicity over data depth.

**What's included:**
- **Open rate & click-through rate** — Standard email performance metrics
- **Subscriber growth chart** — Visual view of list growth over time
- **Broadcast performance** — Per-email stats with comparison to averages
- **Sequence performance** — How each step in an automation sequence performs
- **Revenue tracking** — Basic product revenue attribution
- **Engagement analytics (Pro)** — Subscriber-level engagement scores and behavior patterns
- **Deliverability reporting (Pro)** — Inbox placement rates by email provider
- **Subscriber Signals (Pro)** — Predictive engagement scoring to identify your most valuable subscribers

**What's missing:**
- Revenue attribution per campaign/email
- Heatmaps/click maps showing where subscribers clicked
- Geolocation analytics
- Comparative reporting (period over period)
- Advanced segmentation analytics
- ROI dashboards

For creators who just need to know "are my emails performing well and is my list growing?", Kit's analytics are sufficient. For data-driven marketers who need detailed attribution and optimization insights, the Pro plan or a separate analytics tool is necessary.

### 8. Mobile & SMS Features (86/100)

Kit has made significant strides in mobile features. The platform is fully responsive on mobile devices, and the Creator plan (and above) now includes **SMS marketing**.

**SMS Marketing features:**
- Send text messages to subscribers who have opted in
- Automate SMS sequences alongside email funnels
- Personalize messages with subscriber data
- Track SMS click-through rates
- Compliance with TCPA and CTIA regulations

**Mobile experience:**
- Responsive email rendering (emails look great on any device)
- Mobile-optimized landing pages
- SMS broadcasts from the mobile dashboard
- Subscriber management on the go

SMS marketing is a relatively new addition, and the feature set is more basic than dedicated SMS platforms like Postscript or Klaviyo. However, for creators who want to reach their audience via text without managing a separate tool, it's a valuable addition.

---

---

## Who Is Kit For?

Kit is purpose-built for a specific type of user: **the independent creator**. If you identify with any of the following, Kit is likely the best email marketing platform for you:

- **Bloggers and writers** who send newsletters and want a simple, beautiful way to grow and engage their audience
- **Course creators** who need to nurture leads, launch products, and deliver automated content sequences
- **Podcasters and YouTubers** who want to convert their audience into email subscribers and sell merchandise, books, or premium content
- **Authors** building a reader community, launching books, and running pre-order campaigns
- **Digital product sellers** who want to sell downloads, templates, and printables directly through email
- **Coaches and consultants** building their personal brand and converting followers into clients
- **Solopreneurs and freelancers** who need a simple, reliable email tool without enterprise overhead

### Who Should Look Elsewhere?

- **E-commerce stores** with complex product catalogs — Klaviyo or Mailchimp are better suited
- **Enterprise marketing teams** that need CRM, reporting, and team collaboration at scale — HubSpot or ActiveCampaign
- **Design-heavy brands** that need elaborate email templates with custom HTML — Mailchimp or ActiveCampaign
- **Data-driven marketers** who need detailed attribution and predictive analytics — ActiveCampaign
- **Agencies** managing multiple client accounts — a dedicated enterprise platform like ActiveCampaign or HubSpot

---

## Pricing Breakdown for Real-World Scenarios

### Scenario 1: New Creator (0-1,000 subscribers)
**Best plan: Newsletter (Free) — $0/mo**

Create unlimited landing pages, collect subscribers, tag your audience, send broadcasts, and even sell digital products — all at zero cost. This is the best free plan available for creators.

### Scenario 2: Growing Creator (1,000-5,000 subscribers)
**Best plan: Creator — ~$33-$59/mo (billed yearly)**

Unlock unlimited automations, SMS marketing, A/B testing, and brand removal. At this stage, automations become crucial for nurturing leads and launching products efficiently.

### Scenario 3: Scaling Creator (5,000-25,000 subscribers)
**Best plan: Creator or Pro — ~$59-$167/mo (billed yearly)**

At 5,000+ subscribers, the Pro plan's subscriber signals, engagement analytics, and deliverability reporting become valuable. Collaborative editing and unlimited users make sense if you have a small team.

### Scenario 4: Established Creator (25,000-100,000+ subscribers)
**Best plan: Pro — ~$167-$350+/mo (billed yearly)**

At this scale, the Pro plan's advanced analytics, subscriber scoring, and priority support justify the investment. You're running a serious business and need professional-grade tools.

---

## Final Verdict

Kit (formerly ConvertKit) earns our **93/100 rating** because it excels at what it's designed to do: serve creators who want to build genuine relationships with their audience through email. It's not the most powerful email marketing platform (ActiveCampaign wins that title). It's not the best for beginners (Mailchimp is simpler). But for creators — the specific audience it targets — Kit is unmatched.

**The deciding factors:**
- If you're a creator who values **simplicity, deliverability, and beautiful landing pages**, Kit is your best choice
- If you need **advanced automation, CRM features, and detailed analytics**, ActiveCampaign is a better fit
- If you're a **beginner or e-commerce store looking for templates and ease of use**, Mailchimp is worth considering

Kit's free plan makes it risk-free to try. Start with the Newsletter plan, grow to 1,000 subscribers, and upgrade to Creator when you need automations and SMS. The platform grows with you, and its creator-first philosophy means new features are always designed with your needs in mind.

**Bottom line:** Kit is our top recommendation for email marketing for creators in 2026. It's simple, effective, and built by people who understand what creators need.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is Kit really free?
Yes. Kit's Newsletter plan is completely free for up to 1,000 subscribers with no time limit. You get unlimited landing pages and forms, unlimited email broadcasts, audience tagging and segmentation, and the ability to sell digital products. No credit card required to start.

### What's the difference between ConvertKit and Kit?
ConvertKit rebranded to Kit in 2025. The platform, team, and core features are the same. The name change reflects the product's evolution from a simple email tool into a complete creator business operating system. Existing users were migrated automatically, and all account data, templates, and automations were preserved.

### Does Kit offer a free trial for paid plans?
Yes. All paid plans come with a 14-day free trial. You can explore all Creator or Pro features risk-free. No credit card is required for the free Newsletter plan, but paid plan trials do require payment information.

### Can I sell products directly through Kit?
Yes. Kit has built-in payment processing via Stripe, allowing you to sell digital products, subscriptions, and paid newsletters directly from the platform. Kit handles payment collection, receipt delivery, and subscriber tagging based on purchase behavior.

### Does Kit integrate with WordPress?
Yes. Kit offers a native WordPress plugin that lets you embed signup forms anywhere on your WordPress site. You can also use the embed code method for non-WordPress sites.

### How does Kit's deliverability compare to competitors?
Kit maintains ~97% inbox placement rates, which is among the best in the industry. ActiveCampaign leads slightly at ~98%, while Mailchimp averages ~96%. Kit's proactive sender monitoring and automatic list hygiene contribute to its strong deliverability.

### Can I migrate from Mailchimp or ActiveCampaign to Kit?
Yes. Kit offers free, assisted migrations from Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, and other platforms. Their migration team handles the transfer of subscribers, tags, automations, and templates. Most migrations are completed within 1-2 weeks.

### Does Kit have a mobile app?
Kit offers a mobile-optimized web dashboard but does not have a dedicated mobile app for iOS or Android. You can manage subscribers, send broadcasts, and view analytics from your phone's browser.

### Can I use my own domain with Kit landing pages?
Yes. You can connect a custom domain (e.g., freebie.yourbrand.com) to your Kit landing pages. Custom domain setup is straightforward with DNS configuration instructions provided.

### Is Kit good for team collaboration?
The Pro plan supports unlimited users with role-based permissions and collaborative editing. Lower plans are designed for individual creators and do not include team features.
